issue_context.title: Cannot remove unused variables declared by object destructuring with default value
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

Cannot remove unused variables declared by object destructuring with default value.

However, it works without default value or declared by member accessing with nullish coalescing.

### Input code

```typescript
const { a, b = 'b' } = {};
const c = {}.c ?? 'c';
```


### Config

```json
{
  "minify": true,
  "jsc": {
    "target": "esnext",
    "minify": {
      "compress": {
        "module": true,
        "pure_getters": true
      },
      "mangle": false
    }
  }
}
```


### Playground link (or link to the minimal reproduction)

https://play.swc.rs/?version=1.7.14&code=H4sIAAAAAAAAA0vOzysuUahWSNRRSFKwVVBPUleoBdLVtdZcyWCpZDBPL1nB3l5BPVndmgsAb%2BdTbTIAAAA%3D&config=H4sIAAAAAAAAA32VwXLjIAyG732KjM89dHrYQx9gb30GhoBwyBrwSCJNppN3X5nYadLIuXhsffwSSEL%2Bftlsuj257mPzLa%2FyMVokwOu3WOiU2R7F0oFLlhzGkbvXhe5pQsEOBM10vpCOLfbATUXvb%2B9vs6IbSiFYFLMtxRzD6TamK2lEILqxiVVc1gSZ6V4%2FMyxfE2Cst%2FZtKQPY%2FIQYSyZmhh5Qc%2BzKMNiRwBwsKl6mnVqMVLQQE6wM3oxYRpVnHzmWLDEfqQfrjSseFBQRHMcDaDKJJbJMcjzlPA172Na%2Bb3X%2BpYaDHaplJSYcW0lkt4rXXYnEJtSspfACV3JwgXNyfytjMAhcMT%2Fq9iXmlZr8A5AMDJYo2wSa37YiSD%2BtqcNTZcxBWpZPCpf%2B1k6ZoZekmhiDktkpM4ActWoi%2BOpgyqzTtjPjlfRR9GAgBOkVxTV9RXY7LSifRihBAVJfG7SuugBzvYUrfLoQT%2FBfOSXrDTavSJZ365ROaVuGJwES8K74JwukFFzWMcqUOI7rvGYP0hrg1SWVGngcAnIBuJihzcuH3pDrIR5NP5StOibGikKBGa53YYbn65RONvc%2F0%2BB%2BUKPMwFAw3c5fBOv4fvhizRzT5KOzlYsUIrpuCfSyPJvXLhVfW7j5pzL10%2BVX8Kf7WbRM%2FWuiukifi7Id4%2FwfhUyNrqAGAAA%3D

    Next.js info:

### Expected behavior

All code should be removed.

### Actual behavior

`b` isn't removed.

**Output code**
```js
const { b = 'b' } = {};
```

review_comments: `has_pure_ann` only represents that `init` is pure. Consider that `init` isn't pure, but the `value` is pure
I don't expect such case to exist in real world code
The `value` is an independent and unpredictable expression which inits the value of `undefined` key. I think it has nothing to do with `init`
It's not simply dropping `value`; it's calling `ignore_return_value` on the value because we can drop the initializer.

Yeap.
But if the `init` can't be dropped while the `value` can, this logic will skip dropping `value` because `has_pure_ann` is `false`.
> I don't expect such case to exist in real world code
It's not a real-world code. If there's a code generator tool that's used (not toy) and generates code like that, then it can be a real-world use case.

It's very common but not generated by tool. The example was just from my private project:
```js
const { state = {} } = getRuntimeInfo();
```

`state` is unused after tree shaking, but it cannot be removed.
This is not removable unless pure_getters is true. A member access can have a side effect.
If you are talking about `pure_getters: true`, feel free to send a PR
